'''Timothy John Pedley''' {{post-nominals|size=100%|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 23 March 1942) is a British [[mathematician]] and a former [[G. I. Taylor Professor of Fluid Mechanics]] at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name="ww">{{cite book | title = The International Who's Who 2004 | first = Elizabeth | last = Sleeman | publisher = Routledge | year = 2003 | isbn = 1-85743-217-7 | url-access = registration | url = https://archive.org/details/internationalwho2004ond }}</ref> His principal research interest is the application of [[fluid mechanics]] to [[biology]] and [[medicine]].<ref name=euromech/>

==Early life and education==
Pedley is the son of Richard Rodman Pedley and Jeanie Mary Mudie Pedley. He was educated at [[Rugby School]] and [[Trinity College, Cambridge]].

==Academic career==
Pedley spent three years at [[Johns Hopkins University]] as a post-doctoral fellow.<ref name="ww" /> From 1968 to 1973 he was a lecturer at [[Imperial College London]], after which he moved to the [[Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics]] (DAMTP) at the [[University of Cambridge]]. 

Pedley remained at Cambridge until 1990 when he was appointed [[Professor]] of [[Applied Mathematics]] at the [[University of Leeds]]. In 1996 he returned to Cambridge and from 2000 to 2005 he was head of DAMTP.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/people/t.j.pedley|title=Professor T.J. Pedley|publisher=University of Cambridge Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics|accessdate=2009-07-22}}</ref>

==Research==
Pedley has pioneered the application of [[fluid mechanics]] to understanding biological phenomena. His best-known work includes the study of blood flow in [[artery|arteries]], flow–structure interactions in elastic tubes, flow and [[pressure drop]] in the [[lung]], and the collective behaviour of [[Aquatic locomotion|swimming]] microorganisms.

His research has touched on issues of medical importance, including [[arterial bypass]] [[graft (surgery)|graft]]s, [[urine]] flow from [[kidney]]s to [[bladder]], and the [[Ventilation (physiology)|ventilation]] of premature infants. His work on microorganisms has application to [[plankton]] [[ecology]].<ref name="FRS">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/timothy-pedley-12069|title=Timothy Pedley|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London}} One or more of the preceding sentences may incorporate text from the royalsociety.org website where "all text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." {{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |accessdate=2016-03-09 |url-status=bot: unknown |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160220093712/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archivedate=February 20, 2016 }}</ref>

==Honours==
Pedley is a fellow of [[Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/reporter/2008-09/special/03/11.html|title=Fellows of Gonville and Caius College|publisher=Cambridge University Reporter|accessdate=2009-07-22}}</ref> and was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 1995.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://royalsociety.org/uploadedFiles/Royal_Society_Content/about-us/fellowship/Fellows1660-2007.pdf| title = List of Fellows of the Royal Society 1660 – 2007 | publisher = Royal Society|accessdate = 2012-03-03}}</ref> Pedley was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] (1999) for research on biofluid dynamics, collapsible tube flow, and the theory of swimming of fish and  microorganisms. In 2008 Pedley and [[James D. Murray|Professor James Murray FRS]] were jointly awarded the [[IMA Gold Medal|Gold Medal]] of the [[Institute of Mathematics and its Applications]] in recognition of their "outstanding contributions to mathematics and its applications over a period of years".<ref>{{cite web|title=IMA Gold Medal|url=https://ima.org.uk/awards-medals/ima-gold-medal/|accessdate=16 May 2018}} Institute of Mathematics and its Applications</ref>

He was the 2024 recipient of the Fluid Mechanics Prize of the European Mechanics Society, "for his seminal and outstanding contributions to fluid mechanics applied to biology and medicine, and for his distinguished service and leadership for the European and international fluid mechanics community".<ref name=euromech>{{cite web|url=https://euromech.org/prizes/fluid|title=Fluid Mechanics Prizes|publisher=European Mechanics Society|access-date=2024-04-13}}</ref>

==Marriage and children==
In 1965 Pedley married Avril Jennifer Martin Uden, with whom he has two sons. He enjoys [[birdwatching]], running and reading.<ref name="ww" />
